clue.text: One Mr Bad also awaiting trial

indicators.note: something bad has gone wrong, so the letters of the two words before it are put in a different order

parts.note: also means 'and', as in adding one more thing

explanation.surface: A villainous Mr Bad is locked up waiting for his case to come to court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad' rearranges ONE and MR into ONREM; 'Mr Bad' reads like a villain's name, hiding the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A prisoner held in custody before the hearing is described by this legal phrase.

definitions.meaning: bottle is British slang for courage, an example of the quality of steady boldness
the eye is linked to the brain by a fibre bundle called the optic one

explanation.surface: A bottle hooked up to an optic, the spirit dispenser fixed upside down behind a British bar.
explanation.walkthrough: An optic in a British pub is the measuring dispenser on an upturned spirit bottle, so the surface stays in the bar; the second reading is anatomy.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang uses bottle for courage, and the eye's signal cable to the brain carries this name.

clue.text: Blue material ripped up at ICA

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word for ripped is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: ripped means tore
the ICA is the Institute of Contemporary Arts in London

explanation.surface: Blue material is torn up at a London art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns TORE into EROT; 'at' simply joins it to ICA. The ICA is the Institute of Contemporary Arts, a London gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue is slang for sexually explicit, and material of that kind is writing or art meant to arouse.

indicators.note: among says the letters sit within the run of the words banyan trees

explanation.surface: A tall creature walking among the banyan trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Six-footer' suggests a tall person, but it means a creature with six legs, an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Insects have six legs, so any insect, such as this small colony worker, is a six-footer.

clue.text: Bird makes moves to leave boat

indicators.note: moves says the letters of the two words before it are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: A seabird takes action and flies off a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Passengers getting off a ship at port are said to go ashore in this way.

clue.text: Youngster brought to a Caribbean island

parts.note: a cub is a young animal or a junior Scout

explanation.surface: A child is taken on holiday to a Caribbean island.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest island of the Caribbean, with Havana as its capital.

indicators.note: crossing means the vessel stretches across and so wraps around the river

parts.note: a can is a container
the Po is the great river of northern Italy

explanation.surface: A chicken travels in a boat across a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A castrated cockerel fattened for the table is a kind of domestic fowl.

parts.note: a bar is a pub
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A bird in a pub is now big.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale owl that nests in farm buildings is a common British bird.

parts.note: a go is an attempt, a try
away from home means out

explanation.surface: An order to leave in the hope of a fair hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' reads as a verb but is the noun meaning an attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: A test of a player or product before a decision is a sort of audition or experiment.

clue.text: Grand pubs prepared to welcome monarch

indicators.note: to welcome means the rearranged pubs takes another piece in among its letters
prepared means the letters of pubs are made up in a fresh order

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Fine pubs get ready for a royal visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges the pubs into SUPB, and 'to welcome' means that jumble takes the monarch in; ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the standard crossword Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Grand used as an adjective means splendid or excellent.

indicators.note: guards means the words Chinese military hold the letters inside them

explanation.surface: Soldiers of China stand watch over a home.
explanation.definitionFit: A semi-detached house shares one wall with its neighbour; British speech shortens it to this.

parts.note: a do is a party
a minion is a favoured servant or follower

explanation.surface: A favoured member of the political party now holds office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' suggests politics but is the British word for a social party.
explanation.definitionFit: Sovereign authority over a territory, or rule, is a synonym for power.

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother
a nation is a land or country

explanation.surface: Is there everlasting hell in the motherland?
explanation.definitionFit: Being condemned to hell for ever is the theological sense of the word.

clue.text: Son in tree produces sacred poem

indicators.note: in means the son's letter goes into the tree

parts.note: a palm is a tree

explanation.surface: A boy up a tree comes out with a hymn.
explanation.definitionFit: The Book of the Bible holds 150 of these sacred songs, many attributed to David.

clue.text: Discreet page fronts filthy book collection

indicators.note: fronts means the page comes at the head of what follows

parts.note: filthy jokes are rude
NT, the New Testament, is a collection of books

explanation.surface: A page boy stands at the front of a stash of dirty books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'filthy book collection' reads as one dirty library, but it splits into two pieces; the New Testament counts as a collection because it gathers 27 books.
explanation.definitionFit: Discreet behaviour is careful and wise, which is what this word means.

clue.text: Divine messenger in a new set

parts.note: jelly sets, or gels

explanation.surface: A messenger from heaven appears in a new film or stage set.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavenly beings sent by God to carry news, like Gabriel, go by this name.

definitions.meaning: a start is a beginning or origin
a British rock group formed in 1967, with Peter Gabriel and Phil Collins

explanation.surface: Get going with a rock group.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means origin, from the first book of the Bible, and names a famous progressive rock group.

parts.note: a generous helping is a full one
to back is to support

explanation.surface: A footballer gets lavish backing.
explanation.definitionFit: A defender playing in the deepest position on the side is a type of football player.

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate
a British student who is up is in residence at university

explanation.surface: A learner driver at college makes a howler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a blunder, but here it is a plant that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden plant with tall spikes of pea-like flowers is something that blooms.

definitions.meaning: British slang for arresting a suspect is to collar or pinch them

explanation.surface: Seize Satan!
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for arrest, and Old Nick is a nickname for Satan.

parts.note: a link is a connection

explanation.surface: A Tory politician with ties to someone in jail.
explanation.definitionFit: This is old slang for a jail or lock-up.

clue.text: Oracle's place, quiet in Asian metropolis

indicators.note: in means the letter for quiet goes into the city

parts.note: Delhi is the great city of northern India
p, piano, is the musical mark for quiet

explanation.surface: An oracle's site is a calm spot in a busy Asian city.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek shrine of Apollo, where the Pythia prophesied, stood at this site.

clue.text: Owner of bark in films sails out east

indicators.note: out means the letters of sails are put out of their order

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A sailing ship, bark being a kind of vessel, heads out east in a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bark' looks like a ship to go with 'sails', but it is a dog's bark; the answer is the collie of the films.
explanation.definitionFit: The collie from the 1943 film and its sequels is a screen dog, owner of a famous bark.

parts.note: eg, exempli gratia, means for example

explanation.surface: Talking about length, say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On length' must be split: 'On' is the cricket term for the side of the field behind the batsman's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the on side is also called by this name, the half of the field behind the batter.

indicators.note: returning means the word for lunatics is turned to read backwards

parts.note: nuts are crazy people

explanation.surface: Madmen coming back give everyone a shock.
explanation.definitionFit: To astonish or shock someone is close in sense to surprising them.

clue.text: Ask again for change in Japanese city

indicators.note: for change means the letters of the two words before it are altered in order

explanation.surface: Make a fresh request to visit a city in Japan.
explanation.definitionFit: The port on Kyushu struck by the second atomic bomb in 1945 is a Japanese city.
